title: Headers and query parameters carry a list of values; header names are lower-cased, query names are not.
why: behavioural spec 'request': each is a map of name to a list of values (shape spec §3.6) — a string becomes equality over [value], a list equality over that list, a shape helper an 'each-like' over exactly one value (min 1, max 1, so the dimension has a single point). Header names are lower-cased because HTTP header names are case-insensitive; query names are kept as written because they are not.
